description: This course introduces students to the design and implementation of expert systems using rule-based and case-based reasoning. Topics include knowledge representation with semantic networks and frames; production rule systems like CLIPS and Prolog; forward and backward chaining; inference engines; knowledge acquisition techniques; uncertainty handling with fuzzy logic and Bayes nets; and integration with modern AI frameworks. Students will explore expert system architectures, including the MYCIN and Dendral systems, and apply these concepts through hands-on projects using Python-based tools and industry-standard ontologies.

clos.text: Define the architecture and components of an expert system, including the knowledge base, inference engine, and user interface.
Describe the differences between rule-based and case-based reasoning systems and their respective applications in real-world domains.
Explain the operation of forward and backward chaining algorithms in production rule systems.
Apply fuzzy logic and Bayes nets to model uncertainty in expert systems using Python libraries such as scikit-fuzzy and PyMC3.
Implement a simple expert system using CLIPS or Prolog, demonstrating knowledge acquisition, inference, and user interaction.

topics: History and Evolution of Expert Systems
Knowledge Representation: Semantic Networks and Frames
Production Rule Systems: CLIPS and Prolog
labs: Implement a simple rule-based system in CLIPS
Design an inference engine for a diagnostic application
Model uncertainty in a medical diagnosis system using fuzzy logic
Build a Bayesian network for risk assessment using PyMC3

topics: Expert System Architectures: MYCIN and Dendral

labs: Integrate an expert system with a Python-based NLP pipeline
Develop a case-based reasoning system for customer service
Evaluate an expert system using precision and recall metrics

topics: Ethical and Legal Considerations in Expert Systems
